title: Question about 'As I Was Moving Ahead Occasionally I Saw Brief Glimpses of Beauty'

commenti.body: I saw it only once a year ago, but I am familiar with Mekas' writings (his film journal which I highly recommend to learn about the development of experimental cinema). I would say that in Mekas' perspective, such a film is political because it challenges the aesthetic conventions of mainstream cinema, especially by being extremely personal, and because it is made as an "amateur" film (essentially by Mekas and a few people helping, with a very low budget, without any chances of making a lot of money, etc.)
